messages.body_plain:
Hi,

This is possibly due to a bug present in versions earlier than 1.4.6-p4. The bug caused reads (not read pairs) to be incorrectly counted when the input data are paired end and also stranded.

If you count read pairs (turn on the '-p' option), 1.4.3-p1 and 1.5.0 should give you very similar results. For paired end reads, you should count read pairs since it gives you more accurate counting results.

Sorry about this bug.

Wei

messages.subject: Length calculation wrong for some genes
messages.subject_clean: Length calculation wrong for some genes
messages.body_plain:
I like how fast featureCount is and would like to switch over completely. I have been trying to track down differences in scaling between featureCounts and our previous method (Seqmonk). I have tracked it down to differences in the length of genes reported by featureCounts. For example, here is the line for the Rgs1 (ENSMUSG00000026358) gene using both -g gene_name and without -g option respectively:

Rgs1 chr1 144242296 144249242 - 6947 10990

ENSMUSG00000026358.10 chr1 144242296 144249242 - 6947 10990

They give the same gene length (and counts) but it's far from the expected value of ~1330 base pairs. The refseq line for Rgs 1 lists 5 exons which add up to ~1330. I am using version 1.5.0-p2 with mouse genome GRCm38p3. Both were done with the following command:

featureCounts -a /home/Genomes/GRCm38p3/gencode.vM5.annotation.gtf -s 2 -o 360LA/LA_360Stranded -t exon -g gene_name ...

Here are scatterplots of refseq computed and featurecount reported lengths plotted with a low and medium alpha value to show that most genes are identical but that there are a significant number of outliers.

Peter

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-YteazWExfgY/VzpWEAWcnhI/AAAAAAAAC9M/yLo1_XzV9qEyDFIquRWd5rDa78w5y-yXQCLcB/s1600/Quartz_2____.jpg>

messages.body_plain:
Thanks Wei,
I'm afraid I haven't explained my observation clearly. If anything, the Rgs1 example above (and there are a lot more), go in the opposite direction-- i.e. featureCounts using the Gencode annotation gives a single region whereas the refseq gives five exons. The reason the Gencode gene length is longer is because it doesn't exclude the introns. Here is an image (from seqmonk showing what I mean).

 <https://lh3.googleusercontent.com/-CZbTlQVdqRs/V0NewQXr4iI/AAAAAAAADBI/Z_f2367RT6EFrtZH9gO8Hxl-J9DYaFC4ACLcB/s1600/SeqMonk_.jpg>

For example, Rgs4 is a gene with close correlation between Gencode and refseq. The featurecounts output for that gene is

Rgs4 chr1;chr1;chr1;chr1 169741477;169744351;169745217;169747480 169743920;169744736;169745321;169747642 -;-;-;- 3098 2

The refseq flat file line is:

Rgs4 NM_009062 chr1 - 169741476 169747642 169743680 169747523 5 169741476,169744350,169744674,169745216,169747479, 169743920,169744517,169744736,169745321,169747642,

And the computed length is 2941 bp vs 3098 from featurecounts-- close enough.

Compare this to the featurecount line for Rgs1:

Rgs1 chr1 144242296 144249242 - 6947 10990

with the refseq line:

Rgs1 NM_015811 chr1 - 144244668 144249104 144245301 144249037 5 144244668,144246189,144247905,144248478,144248900, 144245487,144246353,144247967,144248559,144249104,

I agree that Encode should have more features. If I grep the gencode annotation file for ENSMUSG00000026358 (Rgs1), there are 84 lines (not all exons), but somehow featurecount is collapsing all that complexity to a single region for Rgs1 vs the multiple exons found for Rgs4. There should be multiple exons reported for both Rgs1 and Rgs4 but this not the case.

Peter

messages.body_plain:
Hi Wei,

The .featureCounts file created with the -R flag does use the basename of each input BAM file, but they are not saved to the same direcotry as the input files. Consider the following hypothetical featureCounts call:

$ featureCounts -a exons.saf -F SAF -R -o outdir1/outdir2/results.txt indir1/indir2/file1.bam indir1/indir2/file2.bam

The -R flag creates two output files:

outdir1/outdir2/file1.bam.featureCounts
outdir1/outdir2/file2.bam.featureCounts

The description '<input_file>.featureCounts' in the log implies they will be saved to indir1/indir2. I think it would be more informative to output in the log "outdir1/outdir1/<input_file>.featureCounts".

Thanks,

John
